reviews.title: Scam

I am requesting a refund for this purchase.

I purchased credits for InVideo through the App Store, but one single video generation consumed approximately 1,100 credits — essentially my entire monthly credit allowance. The generation took almost two hours and I could not even complete or obtain the finished video.

I was not clearly informed that one single generation could consume my entire monthly allowance. I paid approximately 300 MAD for this purchase and received no completed video in return.

I believe this was highly misleading, and I would like Apple to review this purchase and issue me a refund.

reviews.title: Rating: 1/5 would give 0 - avoid
reviews.text:
I wanted this tool to work, but it is mis‑sold and the service is completely unacceptable. InVideo is operated by Whitesheep Technology Private Limited, based in Mumbai, India – yet it actively markets and sells services directly to UK customers, so it must comply fully with UK consumer law.

I paid for a subscription and extra credits to create professional AI‑animated videos – instead I got static slides with basic zoom/pan effects that even a 16‑year‑old could make using free tools like ChatGPT, Dola, or standard PowerPoint transitions. Their own AI explicitly stated: “You asked for motion graphics and corporate animation – what we have is a slideshow, not animation.” This is not an AI video tool – it delivers nothing you cannot easily do yourself.

The way they handle agreements and compensation confirms this operates like a scam: On 15 June 2026, their manager Tushar formally and unconditionally offered 100 compensatory credits to resolve their service failure. Weeks later, Senior Team Lead Ish and agents Eva and others refused to honour this unless I paid for another subscription, claiming: “We cannot add credits to an inactive account – you must have an active plan first.” This condition was never mentioned at the time of the offer. I never agreed to pay extra just to receive what was already promised and legally owed.

reviews.title: Would give it a 0 if I could
reviews.text:
I genuinely wish I could give 0 stars.

I’ve spent close to £300 trying to create simple children’s educational videos and the experience has been unbelievably frustrating from start to finish.

The platform constantly burns through credits during rendering and exporting, even when videos fail or don’t properly generate. The pricing structure feels extremely misleading because you think you’ve paid enough, then suddenly you’re blocked again by “insufficient credits” halfway through creating/exporting a project.

The mobile app is also incredibly unstable:

* previews don’t load properly
* exports fail
* videos open as black screens
* browser redirects constantly back into the app
* final renders are difficult to access

Even when the AI finally generates a video, the scenes are often inaccurate, inconsistent or completely different from the prompt provided. The marketing makes it seem like you can create polished videos easily, but in reality you still end up spending hours fighting the software.

For the amount of money charged, the experience should be FAR smoother and more reliable.

reviews.title: Total rip-off
reviews.text:
I subscribed to InVideo AI for £20 expecting to be able to actually create videos. What I got instead was one of the most misleading pricing systems I’ve ever seen.

I uploaded just 11 images and a tiny 4-page PDF. That’s it. Somehow, the included credits PLUS an additional purchase of 750 credits still wasn’t enough to generate a usable video. Now I’m being pushed toward paying nearly £100 more just to finish a single project.

This platform is a complete credit black hole.

There is absolutely no transparency about how many credits a video will cost before generation starts. Users are encouraged to begin projects without any realistic understanding of the actual price. By the time you realise how many credits are being consumed, you’re already trapped halfway through a project and pressured into spending more money.

That is concealed pricing, plain and simple.

If generating one short AI video from 11 images and a small PDF can suddenly cost over £100, then users deserve a very clear warning BEFORE they start.

The technology itself may be decent, but the pricing model feels deliberately designed to drain credits as fast as possible while hiding the true cost upfront.

I would strongly advise anyone considering InVideo AI to be extremely careful before spending money. What looks affordable at first very quickly turns into an expensive paywall nightmare.
